title: Early-selected pixel fits increase later dip scatter at 1 and 7 hours in TESS sector 91 of HD 139139
abstract: We test whether an outer-pixel model improves shallow-dip sensitivity at HD 139139 in TESS sector 91. Only early images train the spatial basis. Separate local fit windows test later noise. Five components minimize early depth scatter among 0, 2, 5 and 10 components at box durations of 1, 3 and 7 hours. Later scatter rises by 2.79 and 16.36 percent at 1 and 7 hours, and falls by 1.14 percent at 3 hours. No selected-model later depth crosses six times its early robust scatter. None of 271 later 200-ppm pixel injections passes that threshold with either of two fixed spatial profiles. The fitted depth change remains near the input depth for those profiles. This method does not give a common later noise gain or a strong test for steady K2-like dips. The result is conditional on one aperture, one sector, fixed profiles and known injection times. It does not establish blind-search completeness, a new dip, or a physical cause. Code, source hashes, figures, aggregate results and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Early and later robust depth scatter for four outer-pixel component counts. Local fit windows are separate across the time split.
Box depth estimates with zero and five components. Boundary centers are shown but excluded from selection and later metrics.
